{"answerable":true,"reason":"Aggregate the weekly avg_oil_price (deduplicated per week) and then compute the average per calendar year.","sql":"WITH weekly_unique AS (
    SELECT week_start_date,
           MAX(avg_oil_price) AS avg_oil_price
    FROM weekly_store_family_summary
    GROUP BY week_start_date
)
SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM week_start_date) AS year,
       AVG(avg_oil_price) AS avg_oil_price
FROM weekly_unique
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Aggregate total_sales per store, then select the store with the highest total_sales within each store_type using a row_number window function.","sql":"WITH store_sales AS (SELECT store_type, store_nbr, SUM(total_sales) AS total_sales FROM weekly_store_family_summary GROUP BY store_type, store_nbr) SELECT store_type, store_nbr, total_sales FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY store_type ORDER BY total_sales DESC) AS rn FROM store_sales) t WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY store_type"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Join perishable_volatility_summary and promo_elasticity_summary on store_nbr and family, filter to PERISHABLE series, then compute average empirical_promo_lift_pct and average cv_demand per volatility_proxy_tier.","sql":"SELECT pvs.volatility_proxy_tier,
       AVG(pes.empirical_promo_lift_pct) AS avg_empirical_promo_lift_pct,
       AVG(pvs.cv_demand) AS avg_cv_demand
FROM perishable_volatility_summary AS pvs
JOIN promo_elasticity_summary AS pes
  ON pvs.store_nbr = pes.store_nbr
 AND pvs.family = pes.family
WHERE pvs.perishability_class = 'PERISHABLE'
GROUP BY pvs.volatility_proxy_tier
ORDER BY pvs.volatility_proxy_tier;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Join zero_sales_day_proxy_summary and perishable_volatility_summary on store_nbr and family, filter to HIGH_VOLATILITY_PERISHABLE_PROXY tier, then order by zero_sales_rate_pct descending and limit to 5.","sql":"SELECT z.store_nbr, z.city, z.family, z.zero_sales_rate_pct
FROM zero_sales_day_proxy_summary AS z
JOIN perishable_volatility_summary AS p USING (store_nbr, family)
WHERE p.volatility_proxy_tier = 'HIGH_VOLATILITY_PERISHABLE_PROXY'
ORDER BY z.zero_sales_rate_pct DESC
LIMIT 5"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Sum total_sales by family to get each family's sales, compute overall sales, calculate each family's share of total, order by sales descending and limit to top 5 families.","sql":"WITH family_totals AS (SELECT family, SUM(total_sales) AS family_sales FROM weekly_store_family_summary GROUP BY family), overall AS (SELECT SUM(total_sales) AS total_sales_all FROM weekly_store_family_summary) SELECT ft.family, 100.0 * ft.family_sales / o.total_sales_all AS share_pct FROM family_totals ft CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY ft.family_sales DESC LIMIT 5"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Filter sim_policy_summary for service_level = 0.95 and is_sensitivity_extrapolation = FALSE, then compute the difference in average_inventory_units between the seasonal_naive_safety_stock and lightgbm_point_safety_stock policies for each lead_time_days using conditional aggregation.","sql":"SELECT lead_time_days,
       MAX(CASE WHEN policy = 'seasonal_naive_safety_stock' THEN average_inventory_units END) -
       MAX(CASE WHEN policy = 'lightgbm_point_safety_stock' THEN average_inventory_units END) AS inventory_units_saved
FROM sim_policy_summary
WHERE service_level = 0.95
  AND is_sensitivity_extrapolation = FALSE
GROUP BY lead_time_days
ORDER BY lead_time_days;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Aggregate total_sales by year from weekly_store_family_summary, then use a window LAG to compute the year‑over‑year percentage change for 2015 (vs 2014) and 2016 (vs 2015).","sql":"WITH yearly_sales AS (
    SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM week_start_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
           SUM(total_sales) AS total_sales
    FROM weekly_store_family_summary
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM week_start_date) IN (2014, 2015, 2016)
    GROUP BY year
)
SELECT year,
       total_sales,
       LAG(total_sales) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS prev_year_sales,
       CASE WHEN LAG(total_sales) OVER (ORDER BY year) IS NULL THEN NULL
            ELSE 100.0 * (total_sales - LAG(total_sales) OVER (ORDER BY year)) / LAG(total_sales) OVER (ORDER BY year)
       END AS yoy_pct_change
FROM yearly_sales
WHERE year IN (2015, 6) -- typo intentional? Actually need 2015 and 2016
ORDER BY year;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Aggregate total_sales per week to get chain-wide weekly sales, classify weeks by avg_oil_price < 50 vs >= 50, then count weeks and compute average weekly sales per regime.","sql":"WITH weekly_chain AS (SELECT week_start_date, MAX(avg_oil_price) AS avg_oil_price, SUM(total_sales) AS week_sales FROM weekly_store_family_summary GROUP BY week_start_date) SELECT CASE WHEN avg_oil_price < 50 THEN 'below_50' ELSE '50_or_above' END AS oil_price_regime, COUNT(*) AS num_weeks, AVG(week_sales) AS avg_weekly_chain_sales FROM weekly_chain GROUP BY oil_price_regime"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute average promo_day_share_pct per city and family, select the family with the highest average for each city, then return the top 5 cities alphabetically.","sql":"WITH city_family_avg AS (SELECT city, family, AVG(promo_day_share_pct) AS avg_promo_day_share_pct FROM promo_elasticity_summary GROUP BY city, family), ranked AS (SELECT city, family, avg_promo_day_share_pct, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY avg_promo_day_share_pct DESC) AS rn FROM city_family_avg) SELECT city, family, avg_promo_day_share_pct FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY city LIMIT 5"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Aggregate total_sales by family, compute overall total, select top 5 families by sales and calculate each family's share of the chain-wide sales.","sql":"WITH family_sales AS (
  SELECT family, SUM(total_sales) AS family_total
  FROM weekly_store_family_summary
  GROUP BY family
),
overall AS (
  SELECT SUM(total_sales) AS overall_total
  FROM weekly_store_family_summary
)
SELECT f.family,
       f.family_total,
       (f.family_total / o.overall_total) * 100.0 AS share_pct
FROM family_sales f
CROSS JOIN overall o
ORDER BY f.family_total DESC

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Filter sim_policy_summary for service_level = 0.95 and is_sensitivity_extrapolation = FALSE, then compute the difference in average_inventory_units between seasonal_naive_safety_stock and lightgbm_point_safety_stock for each lead_time_days.","sql":"WITH filtered AS (
